newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dubai crude spreads weaken after India tender.
newsitem.headline: Dubai crude spreads weaken after India tender.

text.p: Dubai intermonth spreads were more than 20 cents lower on Monday from Friday after the state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) awarded just one Dubai cargo in its February buying tender.
February/March Dubai was assessed on Monday in Asia at 45/55 cents per barrel, in from 65/70 cents in Asia on Friday.
March/April was assessed at 55/60, steady from Friday's levels.
The IOC received 10 offers of Dubai cargoes for its buying tender, but traders said it took just one -- from Spain's Repsol at half-month quotes plus 62 cents.
The offers had ranged as high as half-month quotes plus 72 cents, with one offer outside the range at plus $1.00.
Dubai intermonth spreads had remained steady in London from Asia on Friday, but ran up to 70/80 in New York.
Traders estimated that only six cargoes of February Dubai had been placed heading into the India tender.
The tender result could mean that nine cargoes from the tender will be overhanging the market now.
So far, trading in Middle East grades has been brisk with most grades achieving a firm market.
India also awarded three very large crude carriers of Qua Iboe in its February tender.
